description:
P0 mechanics (op-6sl.1) and P1 rheology (op-6sl.2) are both ported and tested,
but nothing wires them together yet. MechanicsSolver still assumes pure linear
elasticity; ConstitutiveLaw::correct is never called.

The rheology port documents exactly what the mechanics layer must do
(rheology/mod.rs, "what the mechanics layer must do"):

1. Pass mechanical strain = total strain MINUS eigenstrain. Passing total strain
   makes an unconstrained, freely expanding pellet look highly stressed -- and it
   will then creep, which is silently and badly wrong.
2. Own one RheologyState per cell.
3. Call correct() repeatedly inside the outer corrector loop from the SAME
   start-of-step state; call advance() ONCE, after convergence. Advancing inside
   the loop double-counts inelastic strain.
4. The corrected stress is softer than the elastic one, so the displacement field
   is no longer in equilibrium -- re-solve with RheologyState::inelastic_strain()
   fed back as an additional eigenstrain (upstream's correctAdditionalStrain).
5. Bound the timestep with CreepTimeStepControl: the creep integration is
   implicit in stress but explicit in state.

Acceptance: a stress-relaxation case where a clamped bar under sustained strain
relaxes toward the creep-equilibrium stress, verified against the closed-form
exponential decay; and a case where free thermal expansion with creep active
produces NO creep strain (the eigenstrain-subtraction check in item 1).

Blocked by nothing -- both halves exist.
title: offbeat: wire rheology into the mechanics solve (inelastic strain feedback, state advance, timestep control)

description:
FOUND 2026-08-11 while doing op-fm5. NOT measured yet -- this is a code-reading finding, so it needs a measurement before it is acted on.

alpha_nightly/controllers/integral_controller/mod.rs, RampResponseRealTime::set_user_input_and_calc (:165-204). The integrator is kept as a line, y(t) = gradient_gain * t + offset, and each input change updates BOTH terms:

    gradient_change = a_i * k_c / tau_i
    offset_change   = -a_i * time_of_input * k_c / tau_i

That is already O(1) per step, so op-fm5 does not touch it. The concern is numerical, not algorithmic: offset accumulates a term proportional to the ABSOLUTE simulation time of every past input change, so for a long-running real-time simulation both 'gradient_gain * t' and 'offset' grow without bound while their SUM stays bounded. That is textbook catastrophic cancellation -- the significant digits available to the integrator output shrink as the run goes on. A real-time twin is exactly the use case where t gets large.

WHAT TO DO:
1. MEASURE FIRST. Drive an IntegralController for, say, 1e6 to 1e8 seconds of simulated time with a changing input, and compare against a Kahan-summed or periodically-rebased reference. Report the actual relative error growth. Do not act on the hunch alone.
2. If confirmed, the fix is to carry the accumulated integral directly (I += k_c/tau_i * u * dt, or the exact ZOH equivalent) rather than reconstructing it from a slope and an intercept, or to rebase the time origin periodically.

Relates to op-fm5 (transfer-function O(1) rewrite) and op-1z3o.14 (real-time execution).
title: chem-eng: IntegralController RampResponseRealTime loses precision on long real-time runs

description:
Found 2026-08-13 while documenting op-yvj.4.8. Pre-existing, not introduced by
that change.

## 1. Broken intra-doc links (24, across at least 5 modules)

cargo doc -p outram-foam-basic-lib --no-deps --release emits 24
'unresolved link' warnings. Unique targets: ComputeBackend (and ::Serial,
::CpuMulti, ::Gpu, ::Auto, ::resolve), ThreadCount, select_backend,
gpu_adapter_present, LduMatrix, bicgstab, bicgstab_prepared, gmres,
gmres_prepared, derived_name, parallel, rayon::ThreadPool::install.

Root cause: lib.rs puts an OUTER /// doc comment on the 'pub mod X;'
declaration while X.rs carries INNER //! module docs. Rustdoc concatenates the
two and resolves the intra-doc links of the merged block in the scope of the
outer item (lib.rs), where none of those names are imported. Every module
carrying both forms is affected -- compute, krylov, ldu_matrix, fv_operators at
minimum.

Why it matters: this is a human-interface-layer defect in the sense the
workspace CLAUDE.md makes mandatory. The module docs are the map a new reader
meets first, and in the rendered docs every type name in them is dead text
rather than a link -- so 'navigable by a Rust developer using rust-analyzer
alone' fails exactly where navigation was supposed to start.

Two candidate fixes, maintainer's choice:
  (a) drop the outer /// summaries from lib.rs and move that text into each
      module's //! header, so links resolve in module scope; or
  (b) keep the lib.rs summaries but make every link in them a fully-qualified
      path (crate::compute::ComputeBackend).
(a) is the smaller diff and keeps one doc home per module; (b) preserves the
at-a-glance module table in lib.rs.

## 2. ComputeBackend::Auto is documented but does not exist

src/compute.rs module docs say callers 'pass [ComputeBackend::Auto]-style
resolution via [select_backend]'. The enum has exactly three variants --
Serial, CpuMulti, Gpu -- and no Auto. Confirmed by reading the enum body.
The sentence should name select_backend/resolve without inventing a variant.
This one is a correctness defect in the docs, not just a dead link, and would
mislead a reader looking for a variant to pass.

Verification: cargo doc -p outram-foam-basic-lib --no-deps --release 2>&1 |
grep -c 'unresolved link'  =>  24, both before and after the op-yvj.4.8 doc
change (checked via git stash).
title: outram-foam-basic-lib: 24 broken intra-doc links in module docs; ComputeBackend::Auto does not exist

description:
The htgr_sim_v1 physics thread in examples/htgr_sim_v1/app/mod.rs advances 10 substeps of PHYSICS_DT_S = 1 ms (10 ms simulated) and then calls thread::sleep(PHYSICS_TICK) with PHYSICS_TICK = 10 ms UNCONDITIONALLY, after the work.

Wall period is therefore compute + 10 ms for 10 ms of simulated time. Real-time ratio = 10/(10+compute_ms). Any nonzero compute makes the sim slower than real time; 1:1 is structurally unreachable, not a tuning question.

Two comments in the file assert the opposite and are wrong:
  - line 42: 'Physics substeps advanced per wall tick (a mild real-time speed-up).'
  - line 159: 'The physics thread runs ~1:1 with wall time (10 substeps of 1 ms per 10 ms tick)'
The tracer animation on line 161-162 is clocked off GUI frame time on the strength of that claim, so tracers run faster than the plant they depict.

Fix: deadline pacing -- record Instant at tick start, sleep PHYSICS_TICK.saturating_sub(elapsed). Also decide and document what should happen when compute exceeds the tick budget (drop to slower-than-real-time and say so in the GUI, vs. reduce SUBSTEPS_PER_TICK).

Why it started mattering today: before edbb2bd7 the steam generator was an algebraic eps-NTU sink and compute was negligible, so the defect was invisible. That commit replaced it with three coupled arrays (OPCPFluidArray + SolidColumn + TampinesSteamArray, 8 nodes, implicit solve, IF97 flashes) on a 0.0125 s substep clock. NOT YET MEASURED: the actual per-tick compute cost, and hence how far off real time it is. Measure before choosing the fix -- the existing test physics::tests::the_whole_plant_steps_at_the_gui_timestep does 20 s of simulated time at 1 ms and its wall clock is a direct read on this.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
DEADLINE PACING LANDED 2026-08-13, following the fhr_sim_v2 pattern per maintainer instruction.

Implementation: new shared crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/app_scaffold/real_time_pacing.rs. Cumulative
plant-clock-vs-wall-clock comparison; ahead -> sleep out the tick budget; behind -> 5 us token sleep and press on.
The cumulative comparison is the valuable part: a stall is WORKED OFF rather than lost. One deliberate deviation from
fhr_sim_v2: the original does not sleep at all on the behind branch, which spins the physics thread against the GUI.

Also fixed here: the two false comments at app/mod.rs:42 and :159, and the tracer animation, which was clocked off GUI
frame time on the strength of the false 1:1 claim and so ran FASTER than the plant it depicts. Tracers now advance on
the delta of snapshot.sim_time_s, which is exact and self-correcting.

Over-budget policy, decided and documented: fall behind, work it off, and SAY SO. Skipping sim time would fabricate
state; growing dt would change the integration. Since panels.rs was reserved for op-qpgw, the readout went on the
schematic -- a 'real-time 0.41x' instrument plus an amber 'SLOWER THAN REAL TIME -- plant clock N.N s behind' line.

Pacer tests (5 new, passing): overrun 25 ms against a 10 ms budget -> 0 ms sleep + 15 ms overrun, where the OLD formula
slept 14 ms; boundary sweep 7-13 ms gave sleeps 3,2,1,0,0,0,0 and overruns 0,0,0,0,1,2,3 with no wrap; a 500 ms stall
cleared in exactly 62 catch-up ticks then resumed sleeping 8 ms.

RESULT: ratio 0.29-0.32 -> 0.41-0.48. DOES NOT REACH 1:1 and cannot -- see op-775s (closed) for the measurement and the
new global-0.1s-timestep bead for the actual route. Not closing this until someone confirms on a display.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
MAINTAINER CONFIRMED ON SCREEN, 2026-08-13: 'it's still slower than real-time, i see the schematic and it works.'

So the INSTRUMENTATION is verified by a human: the real-time ratio readout and the amber 'SLOWER THAN REAL TIME' line
render and report correctly. That was the last thing the headless agent could not check.

DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN. The defect this bead names -- a fixed sleep after the compute instead of a deadline -- IS
fixed (ratio 0.29-0.32 -> 0.41-0.48). But the bead's title claims the physics thread cannot reach real time, and that
is still TRUE: 1:1 is unreachable at dt = 1 ms because the physics costs 2.09-2.45 ms per 1 ms of plant time (op-775s).
Closing it now would read, to anyone scanning closed beads, as though real time had been achieved.

Close this when op-6eqe (global 0.1 s timestep with outer correctors) lands and the measured ratio actually reaches
1:1 -- or reframe the title to name the fixed-sleep defect alone and close it then.

title: htgr_sim_v1: physics thread cannot reach real time -- fixed sleep after compute, not a deadline

description:
FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-14 while wiring light water through to outram-mc.

leapr::generate::generate_tape built S(alpha,beta) by calling ONLY continuous::phonon_expansion (the Fortran 'contin'), then derived dwpix/tempf from the FrequencyModel alone. The Fortran temperature loop (leapr.f90:376-384) runs three stages:

    call contin                       ! continuum
    if (twt.gt.zero) call trans       ! translational term  -> updates tempf (998)
    if (nd.gt.0)     call discre      ! discrete oscillators -> updates dwpix (1388) and tempf (1644)

Both later kernels WERE ported and unit-tested (translation::add_translation, discrete::add_discrete_oscillators, with the correct &mut dwpix / &mut tempf signatures) — generate_tape simply never called them.

Invisible to the graphite validation: crystalline graphite has twt=0 and nd=0, so contin alone IS the whole law. It is severe for any molecular moderator. Measured for H-in-H2O at 293.6 K:

  T_eff          482.49 K  vs published 1194.3 K   (-60%)
  sigma(0.0253)  44.44 b   vs published 52.10 b    (-15%)
  sigma(8 eV)    30.58 b   vs published 20.707 b   (+48%, and NOT decreasing toward the free-atom limit)

After the fix: T_eff 1195.35 K (+0.09%), sigma 52.408 / 21.847 / 21.073 / 20.835 b at 0.0253/1/4/8 eV, all within ~0.6% of the published evaluation.

Also affects every other deck with twt>0 or oscillators: the hydrides, the methanes, ice, D2O, polyethylene. GENERATOR_REVISION bumped 1 -> 2 to invalidate cached artifacts. Regression guard: tests/leapr_h2o_secondary_scatterer.rs::effective_temperature_includes_translation_and_oscillators.
title: njoy leapr: generate_tape skipped the trans and discre stages entirely (molecular moderators badly wrong)
